title: Hyper3D WorldGen builds editable physics worlds from one photo
summary: Announcement thread for Hyper3D WorldGen (Yingmu Technology, CAST/SIGGRAPH 2025): one 2D image becomes an interactive 3D world with per-object meshes, built-in physics, and exports to Blender, Unity, and Unreal — pairable with Seedance for cinematic video on the scene.
question_it_answers: How does WorldGen turn a single photo into editable physics-ready 3D scenes for engines?

claims.text: WorldGen segments a single image into independently movable 3D objects with inferred hidden geometry.
claims.evidence: Feed it a single 2D image, and it picks out every object, fills in the hidden parts, and rebuilds each one as its own separate 3D model
claims.subject: image-to-3d-world

claims.text: Physics collisions, mass, and friction are inferred so objects sit and lean realistically.
claims.evidence: Physics comes built in. It figures out collisions, mass, friction, and how objects actually sit or lean on each other
claims.subject: image-to-3d-world

claims.text: Pairing WorldGen with Seedance 2.5 yields cinematic video from the reconstructed 3D scene.
claims.evidence: pair it with video models like Seedance 2.5, and you get a full pipeline.
claims.subject: ai-video-generation

media.description: Demo video showing a single input photo transformed into an interactive 3D room scene with separately selectable furniture and props.
Follow-up demo clip showing physics interaction and engine export from the WorldGen reconstruction.

judge_hints.why_must_read: One-photo-to-world pipeline that pairs with video models for flythrough production.
